instruction: Work in the Go repository checked out at /echo (module github.com/labstack/echo/v4, Go 1.16). There is exactly one injected BUG in the file /echo/context.go. Hidden tests (not present in the repo) named `TestContext_Scheme`, `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_X-Forwarded-Proto_and_uses_X-Forwarded-Protocol` and `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_forwarded_headers_and_falls_back_to_http` must pass after the fix. The existing test TestContext_Scheme in /echo/context_test.go must keep passing unchanged. Analysis already done: `context.Scheme()` is documented in context.go as 'Scheme returns the HTTP protocol scheme, `http` or `https`'. It currently returns the raw value of the X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme headers without validating it, so an invalid value (e.g. "invalid", "ftp", "https://x") is returned verbatim instead of being ignored. Expected behaviour per the hidden subtest names: an invalid forwarded-header value must be ignored and the next source considered (X-Forwarded-Proto -> X-Forwarded-Protocol -> X-Forwarded-Ssl == "on" -> X-Url-Scheme -> "http"), and if all forwarded headers are invalid the result must be "http". Fix it with a MINIMAL edit (only accept values that are actually the http or https scheme, case-insensitively, and keep the existing precedence and the TLS check). Rules: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; `go test ./...` must stay green; do not edit any file other than /echo/context.go. Verify with a temporary test file (e.g. /echo/zz_tmp_scheme_probe_test.go) covering: X-Forwarded-Proto=invalid + X-Forwarded-Protocol=https -> "https"; all forwarded headers invalid -> "http"; TLS set -> "https"; X-Forwarded-Proto=https -> "https"; X-Forwarded-Ssl=on -> "https"; X-Url-Scheme=https -> "https"; no headers -> "http"; then run `go test ./...` and DELETE the temporary file. Report the exact diff and verification output.

Work in the Go repository checked out at /echo (module github.com/labstack/echo/v4, Go 1.16). There is exactly one injected BUG in the file /echo/bind.go. Hidden tests (not present in the repo) named `TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap` and `TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap/ok,_bind_to_map[string][]string` must pass after the fix. Analysis already done: `(*DefaultBinder).bindData` has a map-destination branch that does `val.SetMapIndex(reflect.ValueOf(k), reflect.ValueOf(v[0]))` for every map type. That means (a) it panics for a nil map, (b) it panics when the map value type is not string (e.g. a `map[string][]string` destination: 'reflect.Set: value of type string is not assignable to type []string'), and (c) it silently drops all but the first value. Expected behaviour: binding into a `map[string][]string` destination must work and must store the full slice of values for each key; binding into `map[string]string` must keep the current behaviour (first value); unsupported map types must return an error instead of panicking. Fix it with a MINIMAL edit to /echo/bind.go only. Rules: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; `go test ./...` must stay green (especially TestBindbindData and TestBindForm/TestBindQuery etc.); do not edit any other file. Verify with a temporary test file (e.g. /echo/zz_tmp_bind_probe_test.go) that calls `new(DefaultBinder).bindData` with: &map[string]string{} -> first value; &map[string][]string{} -> full slice; a nil map[string][]string; a map[string]int{} -> error not panic; then run `go test ./...` and DELETE the temporary file. Report the exact diff and verification output.
